page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.large is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, running on a KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, provisioned with 1 physical CPU core, 2 hyperthreads, and 2 vCPUs under a shared CPU allocation model. The instance features 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM balance with 4.0 GB per core. It includes 35 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware support for instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, and AES. It includes no attached local NVMe storage and zero discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations position the ecs.mn4.large instance in lower performance tiers relative to dedicated compute options. Single-core processing registered a stress-ng score of 1090.78 and a Geekbench single-core score of 939.0, both falling within the bottom 25 percent of evaluated cloud hardware. Multi-core compute performance sits in the bottom 10 percent, marked by a stress-ng multi-core result of 2067.18 and a PassMark CPU score of 2646.42. Uncached memory throughput measures 16.93 GB/sec for reads and 13.99 GB/sec for writes. The shared CPU allocation introduces potential compute contention during sustained resource utilization, representing a key hardware tradeoff.

Given its 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and shared CPU architecture, ecs.mn4.large offers entry-level resource density. The provision of 8.0 GB RAM across 2 vCPUs makes it a practical option for workloads where execution speed is secondary to memory capacity. It is suitable for lightweight web applications, entry-level microservices, staging environments, basic Redis caching, and non-critical background jobs with low CPU usage demands.
